headline: The most significant changes on the P-1 prototype focus on aerodynamics and low observability. Enlarged ailerons reduce the wing-to-tip transition angle, lowering the aircraft's front-aspect radar cross-section (RCS). Continuity with the flaperons has also been improved, while the outer wing-edge break has been eliminated. The air intakes have been moved farther aft and widened, improving aerodynamics, reducing RCS, and providing better shielding of the engine fan blades. The wider intakes may also prepare the airframe for Turkey's indigenous TF-35000 engine. The vertical stabilizers (green rectangle, top image) appear to incorporate conformal electronic warfare (ECM) systems in their leading edges, a feature previously seen on the latest Kızılelma prototype. The nose has been redesigned with more space for an IRST (Infrared Search and Track) system, while the radome has been shortened along the longitudinal (X) axis. Symmetrical Turkish EOS (Electro-Optical System) sensors have also been added ahead of the canopy. The aircraft now features a reverse-opening canopy, similar to the F-35A and J-35. Although it offers only a modest reduction in RCS, it reflects efforts to further reduce the aircraft's radar signature. At the rear, RAM (Radar-Absorbent Material) has been applied around the engine nozzles to protect against exhaust heat and reduce the infrared signature. The engines have also been spaced farther apart, creating a gap comparable to that of the Su-57, which may house a radar or electronic warfare equipment.

headline: The U.S. Navy has reclassified future Virginia class attack submarines equipped with the Virginia Payload Module (VPM) as guided missile submarines (SSGNs), formally recognizing their expanded strike role as the service prepares to retire its four Ohio class SSGNs by the end of 2029. The VPM adds four large payload tubes, increasing a Virginia-class submarine's Tomahawk capacity from 12 to 40 missiles while also enabling future deployment of Intermediate-Range Conventional Prompt Strike (IRCPS) hypersonic missiles and other payloads. The Navy says it plans to field 19 Virginia SSGNs, with the first expected to be USS Arizona. The redesignation reflects the Navy's plan to preserve long-range undersea strike capability, but The War Zone notes the new submarines are not one-for-one replacements. An Ohio-class SSGN can carry up to 154 Tomahawk cruise missiles, roughly the equivalent of four Virginia SSGNs in missile capacity alone. With the final Ohio-class SSGN scheduled to retire years before all 19 Virginia SSGNs enter service, the Navy is expected to face a prolonged reduction in undersea strike capacity during the transition, according to The War Zone.

headline: The Department of War has signed new framework agreements with Northrop Grumman and Lockheed Martin aimed at dramatically expanding U.S. interceptor production, increasing PAC-3 Patriot Missile Segment Enhancement (MSE) capacity from about 600 missiles per year to 2,000 per year, while expanding THAAD interceptor production from 96 to 400 interceptors annually. The agreements are designed to strengthen the missile defense industrial base by establishing a second source for PAC-3 solid rocket motors, expanding production of ignition safety devices, and increasing output of critical THAAD structural components to create a more resilient supply chain. The announcement comes after months of reporting from The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times, Reuters, and The Washington Post that the Iran war has sharply increased demand for Patriot and THAAD interceptors, with senior U.S. military leaders warning that sustained operations have placed growing pressure on both interceptor inventories and the industrial base needed to replenish them.

headline: President Trump is considering removing U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro after the Justice Department concluded that problems with the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool resulted from a flawed renovation rather than vandalism, according to people familiar with the matter. Trump publicly criticized Pirro on Monday, saying he was "really disappointed" and that she "folded like an umbrella" after the Justice Department moved to dismiss the criminal case tied to the Reflecting Pool. CNN reports the president was "furious" over the filing, believes he was not informed in advance, and is now weighing whether to remove one of his longtime political allies from the position. The Justice Department's filing stated the evidence no longer supported the prosecution after determining the damage stemmed from construction issues rather than criminal vandalism, according to CNN.
